city_center.name: Brooklyn brownstone belt (Brooklyn Heights / Park Slope) + Manhattan Union Square Greenmarket
city_center.landmark: Union Square Greenmarket (est. 1976, four days/week); Brooklyn brownstone stoops; the bodega on every corner
city_center.notes: GrowNYC's Union Square Greenmarket is the flagship of the city's farmers-market network, running four days a week year-round. Brooklyn's signature residential fabric is 19th-century brownstone rowhouses. The corner bodega is the everyday neighborhood grocery. sources: grownyc.org; en.wikipedia.org Brownstone / Bodega (store).

cultural_notes: the corner bodega is the everyday New York neighborhood grocery -- a cultural fixture especially across Brooklyn, the Bronx, and Manhattan (source: Bodega (store), en.wikipedia.org)
GrowNYC Greenmarkets bring regional Hudson Valley / upstate producers into the city; Union Square is the flagship, running four days a week (source: grownyc.org)

Brooklyn's brownstone rowhouse belt (Brooklyn Heights, Park Slope, Bed-Stuy, Fort Greene) is a defining architectural identity -- 19th-century brown Triassic sandstone facades and stoops (source: Brownstone, en.wikipedia.org)
New York apartment life leans on grocery delivery and small-format shopping; weekend brunch is a strong occasion (source: general market framing, publicly documented)
